conclusion: REMOVES the two outstanding confounds in the paper-2 cross-engine headline at once. Run on the SAME beta=40 / n=89 / mt=50 / q-grid as the g6k onset record, under the IDENTICAL reference-free DSD criterion (b1=min(gs)>1.5). The SD-BKZ DSD-onset gap reproduces on the fplll enumeration engine: at q=137 SD cracks DSD on 8/20 seeds vs BKZ 1/20 (gap +7), while g6k shows 14/4 (gap +10) at the same cell. Same onset location (q~137), same direction (SD reaches dense-sublattice discovery at lower q than BKZ), same magnitude scale (+7 enum, +10 sieve). q=157 both nearly saturate (SD still ahead, +2 / +1); q>=181 both crack on all 20. The mean signed d(LN) advantage goes large-negative exactly where SD fires DSD (fplll -21.93 at q137, mirroring g6k -30.83) -- the signed-d(LN)-is-a-reference-artifact finding, now shown on BOTH engines. Net: the gap is NOT a beta=20 artifact (both engines at beta=40) and NOT an engine artifact (enum AND sieve). It is a property of self-dual reduction reaching DSD earlier in q.
